pairs.subject: deployment-contract
pairs.evidence: scripts/deploy/check-chart.mjs:34 The Helm chart policy this context owns runs only in ci.yml. The tag-triggered release path (.github/workflows/release.yml: gate → publish → release, which runs `helm package deploy/helm/kp` at line 285) never runs deploy:check, even though its header calls its gate job "the full verification gate, again, on the tagged commit". So the chart that gets published is not certified by the chart verdict on the path that publishes it.

techniques.evidence: scripts/deploy/check-chart.mjs:34 Publishing is mechanically coupled to a gate (publish needs: gate), and release:check is part of that gate. But deploy:check/test:deploy are absent from release.yml, so a tag (which can sit on a commit main's CI never judged) packages and releases the chart without this verdict. The re-run gate is a subset of what it claims to be.

scripts/deploy/check-chart.mjs:529 The deployment shape is a committed chart, and the env contract is checked in both directions: every key the chart sets must be documented in .env.example (names only), and the required keys must stay set. Secret values are kept out of values.yaml by the secret-literal-in-values policy.

scripts/release/prepare.mjs:150 The host (Kubernetes via Helm) builds nothing; it pulls the CI-built image, which is the prebuilt escape. release:check keeps the chart's image tag in lockstep with package.json and the CHANGELOG.

scripts/release/prepare.mjs:15 The chart only pulls an image tag. One build (docker/build-push-action in release.yml) sends one context, so there is no second remote upload filter to keep in parity. This is the technique's own 'when not to use it' case.

scripts/deploy/check-chart.mjs:227 The chart deploys the live, authenticated product rather than a public demo. The policy forces a `required` password and forbids shipping KP_ALLOW_OPEN on, which is the technique's 'needs authentication, not a mode' exclusion.

pairs.registryProposal: deploy-gate-coupling could state that resolution one (deploy waits for the gate) also covers a gate RE-RUN on the release trigger: a tag-path gate that re-runs only a subset of the push-path gate, and drops the checks over the very artifact it publishes (here, the Helm chart), reopens the race on exactly those checks. That is the mirror of the local-vs-remote parity invariant the technique already names for resolution two.
